newsitem.title: CANADA: Indochina buys into Kazakhstan gold mine.
newsitem.headline: Indochina buys into Kazakhstan gold mine.

text.p: Indochina Goldfields Ltd said on Monday it had agreed to buy a 15 percent direct stake in the Bakyrchik gold mine in eastern Kazakhstan.

The company said the transaction is part of the first full privatization of a major government-controlled gold mine in Central Asia. The deal was made possible by the Kazakhstan government's decision to sell its 60 percent interest in the Bakyrchik joint venture.
The joint venture will become the 100 percent owner of the entire mine complex, Indochina said in a release.

Indochina will buy from London-based Bakyrchik Gold Plc a 15 percent direct interest in the joint venture. Bakyrchik Gold, which has owned 40 percent of the joint venture since 1992, will increase its holding to 85 percent.
Indochina is Bakyrchik Gold's biggest shareholder, owning 26.3 percent of Bakyrchik Gold.
The deal will give Indochina a combined 37 percent direct and indirect interest in the gold property, which has a resource of more than 10.5 million ounces, Indochina said.
The government will receive a total of US$60 million for its interest, plus a US$5 million signing fee.
Indochina said it has already paid the US$5 million and an initial installment. The remaining balance of US$45 million is the responsibility of Bakyrchik Gold, Indochina said.
Indochina will provide Bakyrchik Gold with a US$20 million loan.
Indochina Goldfields and Bakyrchik Gold will be responsible for pro rata costs and will receive revenue in porportion to their participating interests, Indochina said.
"This is a termendous opportunity for Indochina Goldfields to play an important role in the development of a world-scale deposit," company president Edward Flood said.
"We've gone from being a passive investor to an active participant in what willl be one of the largest gold producers in Central Asia."
